name: Bald Knobber graves: Dave & Billy Walker
where: Abundance Cemetery, near Sparta, Christian County. I could not find coordinates for the cemetery, so the circle is centered on Sparta.
story: Father and son hanged with John Mathews in Ozark on May 10, 1889, after a botched gallows. The last act of the Christian County Bald Knobbers.
access: Cemetery access unknown. Ask the landowner if it's on private land.

name: Mathews Cemetery (John Mathews lead)
where: Mathews Cemetery near Chadwick, Christian County (USGS coordinates).
story: UNCONFIRMED LEAD. John Mathews was the third Bald Knobber hanged in 1889, and the Christian County group was centered on Chadwick. I found no source saying where he is buried. This family cemetery is a lead, not a match.

name: Snapp Balds: Bald Knobbers' first meeting place
where: Just north of Kirbyville, Taney County. USGS marks Snapp Balds as a ridge range; the exact meeting knob isn't pinned.
story: Where Nat Kinney's Taney County vigilantes first met. The open bald knobs let them watch for spies, and gave the group its name.

name: Murder Rock: Alf Bolin's ambush spot
where: Rock outcrop on the old Springfield–Harrison road, about 8 miles from Hollister, Taney County (USGS coordinates).
story: Civil War bushwhacker Alf Bolin reportedly hid in these rocks to rob and kill travelers on the road. Look for the old roadbed beside it in the LiDAR.
access: PRIVATE. Owner proposed public access in 2020; status unknown since. Don't go without permission.
search: Murder Rock Alf Bolin Taney County

sources.t: KY3: Murder Rock could open to the public (2020)

name: Layton's Mill: Bolin gang hideout area
where: About 3 miles south of Murder Rock, near the Arkansas line. The circle is placed from that distance alone.
story: An 1862 Union report put Bolin's band in the hills toward 'Laten's Mills'. The mill is long gone.
search: Layton Mill Taney County Alf Bolin

sources.t: Ozarks History: Alf Bolin, just facts

name: Clark's Mill battle & blockhouse
where: On Bryant Creek about a mile north of Vera Cruz, Douglas County. Placed from that description.
story: Union blockhouse captured and destroyed in the Nov. 7, 1862 battle. A 2012 report says traces of the old Vera Cruz Road are still visible on the farm. Good LiDAR target.
search: Clark's Mill battle Vera Cruz Douglas County

sources.t: KSMU: landowner finds his farm was a battle site (2012)

name: Vera Cruz: lost first county seat
where: On Bryant Creek, central Douglas County (USGS coordinates).
story: Douglas County's first seat until 1870, with a courthouse, mills, blacksmith and about 15 homes. Now only a cemetery and an old log church remain. Building pads and the old mill pond may show in LiDAR.
search: Vera Cruz Douglas County Missouri history

name: Breadtray Mountain: Spanish silver legend
where: Summit near Table Rock Lake, Stone County (USGS coordinates). The legend gives no spot on the mountain.
story: Centuries-old tale of Spanish explorers sealing a silver mine here. Unproven. Old prospect pits or diggings might show on the slope layer.
access: Ownership not checked. Confirm before going; no digging on public land.

sources.t: State of the Ozarks: Legend of Breadtray Mountain
